svg.aria-label: How each guide moves through review
svg.title: How each guide moves through review
svg.text: How each guide moves through review
One writer, eleven cold editors in a fixed order, two script gates, two human decisions.
code block rerun, its output compared
LINE AND FIGURES: how it is said
fixes add words; the same checks
SERIES: agree with the other eleven?
each editor, rounds, verdict, open findings
One agent in the main conversation. It drafts,
runs every code block, starts each editor as a
cold subagent (file paths in, verdict out),
applies the findings it accepts, and logs each
decision in reviews/<slug>/. It never reviews
its own guide and never marks one as shipped.
Each finding is accepted or rejected against
the house style, with a one-line reason in
When two editors could flag the same thing,
the owner flags it and the other stays silent:
wrong numbers to accuracy, em-dashes to slop.
purpose, reader, outline, word budgets, done-when test
simplifications, and where each is repaid
the example traced through all 12 guides
Each editor returns SATISFIED or NOT SATISFIED with up to ten quoted findings, ranked
HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW. SATISFIED means no HIGH and at most two MEDIUM.
The writer revises and re-sends, for at most three rounds. At the limit, the summary says
so beside the verdict and the open findings go to the author.
Nothing enforces the order except the writer's instructions and the files each stage
leaves behind. The gate is the only check that is code.
Across the series: 12 guides, 131 first-round reviews (77 SATISFIED on the first read),
about 200 editor rounds, every one of them run in sequence.
